bullets.title: The King of Kong
bullets.note: This doc was originally recommended to me by the world’s most interesting man, [Kevin Kelly](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/75u8wd0mmu8h07opxh9/zefghnhko53g8m/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDE0LzA4LzI5L2tldmluLWtlbGx5Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWNvbnZlcnRraXQmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1jb252ZXJ0a2l0JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj01YmY=). I’ve watched it every year or two since. The movie is like a real-life _Spinal Tap_ about becoming king of the nerds. Trust me; it’s well worth the watch. Here’s a shortened description: “In the early 1980s, legendary Billy Mitchell set a Donkey Kong record that stood for almost 25 years. This documentary follows the assault on the record by Steve Wiebe, an earnest teacher from Washington who took up the game while unemployed.”

bullets.title: Dustin Yellin
bullets.note: ([@dustinyellin](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/75u8wd0mmu8h07opxh9/k5cmh6h58zl737/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9kdXN0aW55ZWxsaW4v)). Dustin is a contemporary artist best known for sculptural paintings that use multiple layers of glass, each covered in detailed imagery, to create a single, intricate, three-dimensional collage. His work is notable both for its massive scale and its fantastic, dystopian themes. Yellin is the founder of Pioneer Works ([@pioneerworks](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/75u8wd0mmu8h07opxh9/q9s8h7h48erx67/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9waW9uZWVyd29ya3Mv))—a not-for-profit cultural center in Red Hook, Brooklyn—where I [originally discovered his work](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/75u8wd0mmu8h07opxh9/95azhnh6g4p726/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuaW5zdGFncmFtLmNvbS9wL0Jia0hrdU1GZ0JOLw==).
